description:
## Goal

An unchanged request should reuse everything and do essentially no compiler work. An unrelated edit should invalidate nothing for the requested root. A relevant edit should recompute only the exact transitive dependents of what changed.

## Priorities, in order

1. Correct semantics by construction. One denotation, one identity, exact ownership, typed comparisons, and no display strings or incidental ordering acting as authority.
2. Collapse duplicate concepts and authorities. One World fact authority and one retained ProductMemo authority. Delete parallel stores, scanners, bridges, private cones, compatibility paths, and redundant telemetry.
3. Make work edge-triggered. Work begins only because a precise source, fact, product, demand, or dependency edge moved—not because the compiler rescanned global state.
4. Retain and share results. Equal reproduction preserves the existing allocation and generation, wakes nobody, and performs no deep copies.
5. Make cycles ordinarily reactive. Monotone formulas converge through the normal dependency scheduler, replacing private SCC/fixpoint/cone mini-compilers.
6. Make native compilation body-incremental. Changed bodies alone trigger lowering/codegen; unchanged bodies and whole-root products are reused.
7. Own source replacement exactly. Withdraw obsolete contributions and reclaim superseded snapshots without losing diagnostics or correctness.
8. Prove less work deterministically. Causal counts, evaluations, generations, allocations, compile counts, and byte-identical artifacts are authoritative. Wall-clock and CI duration are corroborative signals, not substitutes.
9. Leave no construction debris. Temporary probes, adapters, duplicate tests, migration scaffolding, old documentation, and obsolete concepts must disappear after each cutover.

## Ultimate acceptance

Same input means reuse; unrelated change means no work; relevant change means only necessary work—while preserving every semantic answer and artifact.

## Current signal at origin/main a3a9761d1

Representative 00420 evidence:

- 2,381 scheduler completions and 9,809 product settlements.
- RuntimeDemand cone settlement reaches 204 members, 17 rounds, and 1,068 member derivations; sampling places roughly one quarter of captured main-thread stacks in runtime-demand production.
- 4,094 TransportShape plus 3,901 CallableConstruction settlements are 81.5 percent of product settlements.
- The activation frontier reaches 66 entries; 918 completions occur while it is nonempty.
- Identical callee input rows repeat up to 26 times in one conclusion.
- 206 each of Materialized, ABI, and Backend products cause at least 2,472 deep executable-tree clone passes before whole-program handoff clones.
- Direct native lowering visits 204 backend executables and takes about 616 ms in the debug trace bracket; fresh native codegen takes about 3.19 seconds and defines 943 functions.
- The public root_scans counter is always zero because its sole producer has no callers; it does not observe the real scans.

Timings are diagnostic leads. Acceptance uses exact evaluations, settlements, generations, clones/allocations, dependency movement, and byte-identical artifacts.

## Strategy: work backward from exact reuse

### 1. Remove work with no production consumer

- fz-tfn.3: delete test-only output aggregation paid on every scheduler completion.
- fz-tfn.17: delete constant backend/native revision fields.
- fz-tfn.4: delete the retired SettledPresence mode after current causality work.
- fz-tfn.7: delete the end-session executable-effect audit after its invariant is pinned.

### 2. Make scheduler work edge-triggered

- fz-tfn.5 deletes the duplicate standing-root scanner.
- fz-kdt.46 replaces wait inventories with exact wait edges.
- fz-tfn.6 replaces activation-frontier scan/sort/reinsertion with exact Activation appearance edges.
- fz-tfn.15 then deletes the misleading scan canary; fz-tfn.16 replaces fixed HashMap accounting.
- fz-kdt.7 makes subscription replacement proportional to changed memberships.
- fz-kdt.49 and fz-kdt.114 remove or retire execution-order sorting after the edge cutover.

### 3. Delete duplicate semantic work and identity

- fz-kdt.72 removes identical input contributions before joins.
- fz-0za then fz-tfn.14 and fz-tfn.19 replace the orphan generic contribution model with explicit, change-aware activation input storage.
- fz-kdt.182 then fz-kdt.48 establish one Ty per denotation, preventing duplicate activation/product/native identities.
- fz-kdt.68 must either pay for per-answer derivations or delete the dormant derivation substrate; latent precision is not retained for free.

### 4. Make product state singular, shared, and reactive before persistence

Two branches follow the causality baseline:

- fz-tfn.7 -> fz-tfn.8: replace the ExecutableEffects cone/SCC/snapshot/reverse-graph mini-compiler with one reactive formula per executable.
- fz-tfn.9 shares immutable product payloads.

Reactive effects and shared payloads converge on fz-tfn.10, which deletes PullSession's remaining parallel artifact maps. That singular ProductMemo authority then enables fz-tfn.1 to persist one exact product calculation per root. This ordering prevents the long-lived design from freezing deep-copy bookkeeping or duplicate authorities into retained state.

Then:

- fz-kdt.4 replaces RuntimeDemand cone replay.
- fz-kdt.57 makes root transport relations react to exact edge changes.
- fz-kdt.58 prunes unjustified transport/callable products.
- fz-tfn.18 decomposes whole-root packaging into exact shared contributions.

### 5. Make native compilation incremental

- fz-tfn.17 and fz-tfn.1 enable fz-tfn.11, which makes NativeProgram a retained root product and deletes direct LowerNativeProgram execution/fact storage.
- fz-tfn.12 moves macro roots to persistent products and deletes the remaining BackendProgram scheduler bridge.
- After denotational and callable-key work, fz-tfn.13 gives native bodies stable identities and reuses codegen by changed generation.

### 6. Bound long-lived source state

fz-kdt.24, fz-kdt.30, and fz-kdt.32 establish exact function/module/requester ownership. fz-tfn.20 then withdraws and reclaims superseded source snapshots and subscriptions without losing diagnostics.

## Dependency shape

```mermaid
graph LR
  C[Causal baseline] --> A[Share immutable payloads]
  A --> S[Delete parallel product stores]
  C --> E[Delete effect auditor]
  E --> R[Reactive executable effects]
  R --> S
  S --> P[Persistent root sessions]
  P --> D[Reactive RuntimeDemand]
  D --> T[Exact transport relations]
  T --> U[Prune unjustified products]
  U --> G[Exact root packaging]

  Q[Delete root scanner] --> X[Exact activation edges]
  W[Exact wait edges] --> X
  X --> M[Delete false scan metric]
  W --> M

  N[Denotational Ty identity] --> J[Incremental native bodies/codegen]
  P --> L[NativeProgram product]
  L --> B[Delete backend fact bridge]
  L --> J
```

## Execution protocol

Each child is one proof, one commit, and one close after a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review. Reviewed commits continue on draft epic PR #118, stacked above semantic-correctness PR #110 through GitHub stack #120; push each completed boundary for interim review only after the preceding pushed head has green CI. Work may begin on the next ready ticket while CI runs. Implementation is delegated per ticket and bw ready fz-tfn drives dependency order. Every PR is reviewed against its branch root and has a title beginning with its ticket id. Temporary counters, A/B switches, oracle fixtures, and migration tests leave at their cutover; necessary transition affordances have explicit deletion tickets.

## Completion

- Unchanged requests evaluate no settled formula/product/native body and perform no deep artifact copy.
- Unreachable edits invalidate/evaluate nothing for the root.
- Reachable edits evaluate only the exact transitive reader closure.
- No normal-drive global discovery scan, cone replay, private fixpoint, duplicate product store, or unconditional whole-root native phase remains.
- Semantic answers, diagnostics, canonical artifacts, ABI, and runtime behavior retain full fidelity.
- northstar.html, agent docs, and user guides describe only implemented ownership and scheduling.
- Full library, single-threaded fixture matrix, interp/run/build parity, cross-process determinism, formatting, and clippy with warnings denied pass.
title: Compiler2: eliminate batch work and become a long-lived recalculator
